key_insight: A single end-to-end model can turn 3D cardiac CT/MRI directly into a smooth, simulation-ready mesh, bypassing manual segmentation and post-processing.
clinical_relevance: This could speed creation of patient-specific cardiac digital twins for planning and simulation by reducing dependence on specialized mesh-cleaning workflows.
method: 3D Swin Transformer encoder-decoder extracts volumetric features from CT/MRI.
Graph Attention Network (GAT) deforms a template mesh to match the cardiac surface.
Direct single-pass pipeline removes Marching Cubes, smoothing, and manual cleanup.
evidence_signal: On the MM-WHS 2017 benchmark, the model reported Dice scores of 0.84 on CT and 0.83 on MRI, with mean Chamfer distance of 1.8 mm and 95th-percentile surface distance below 5 mm.
watch_item: Results come from a benchmark setting, so real-world robustness, anatomy generalization, and integration into clinical workflows still need validation.
paper_title: Transformer-Guided Graph Attention for Direct Cardiac Mesh Reconstruction: A Structural Digital Twin Framework
